chapters.line: It plays by itself at night. Always his tune. He hated that tune.

outcome_lines.done: Bless you. The house will be so quiet. I shan't know what to do.
outcome_lines.refused: No? Then we'll hum along, the two of us. Badly.

chapters.line: It was on my pillow this morning. You did buy it, didn't you? Nod.

outcome_lines.done: Gone again. I'll check the pillow anyway. Habit.
outcome_lines.refused: Back in the drawer. It does look pleased with itself.

chapters.line: It is lonely, I think. Have you a toy to sit beside it?

outcome_lines.done: Perfect. They get on famously. It plays two tunes now.
outcome_lines.refused: Fine. I'll make it a friend from old socks.

chapters.line: It stopped last night. His tune, once, then a little goodbye.

outcome_lines.done: Keep it. It is only a box now. A kind one, mind.
outcome_lines.refused: Then it stays. Quiet at last, and I shall miss the racket.

chapters.line: Grandpa's voice is in the horn. He keeps asking if I've done my sums.

outcome_lines.done: Thanks! Now who'll check my sums? Oh no. Nobody. Hooray?
outcome_lines.refused: Fine. I'll do the sums. He gets so smug about it.

chapters.line: Grandpa wants to know where everything is now. Any book of maps?

outcome_lines.done: He says your shop is a bit left of Heaven. That's good, I think.
outcome_lines.refused: He'll have to guess. He guesses terribly. We keep ending up in Ohio.

chapters.line: He's started singing hymns through the horn. Off key. All night.

outcome_lines.done: Now he can't read the words. He's humming. It's an improvement.
outcome_lines.refused: Then he'll keep singing. The cat has started to harmonise.

chapters.line: He said he's proud of me, then went quiet. It's just a horn now.

outcome_lines.done: He'd want it to go to a good home. Wind it up sometimes.
outcome_lines.refused: Then I'll keep it. I like the quiet. I like it a bit less each day.

chapters.line: I wagered a hand bell with something in my cellar. At cribbage. It cheats.

outcome_lines.done: Politely, mind. It apologises when it pegs out. Take the bell.
outcome_lines.refused: Then I'll lose it in the next game. Pray for my cribbage.

chapters.line: I need a clock that runs slow, or some relic that stalls time.

outcome_lines.done: Always ten to midnight. I am winning. I may be sinning. Splendid.
outcome_lines.refused: Then I'll play on. It's up forty hymns and a pew.

chapters.line: It won my pocket watch. It says it will give it back for a tuning fork.

outcome_lines.done: Ha! It hummed and the cards all stood up. Cheating, but pretty.
outcome_lines.refused: Then I'll bluff. I have never once bluffed. This will be dreadful.

chapters.line: It conceded. It wants a rematch Thursday, and it is sending a hamper.

outcome_lines.done: For the cellar, so it can see its cards. We are friends now, God help us.
outcome_lines.refused: Then I shall play in the dark. It will be easier to look innocent.

chapters.line: My assistant is still in this box. In the trick, I mean. Mind the lid.

outcome_lines.done: Splendid. She's comfortable. Don't feed her. She's on a diet.
outcome_lines.refused: Pity. Applause is the only wage she accepts.

chapters.line: I need a mirror or some such relic for the act. She checks her hair.

outcome_lines.done: She says thank you. From inside. It's muffled but it's sincere.
outcome_lines.refused: Then she'll fix her hair by feel. Please don't tell her it's crooked.

chapters.line: She keeps swapping places with this marionette. I can't tell which is which.

outcome_lines.done: One of you is a puppet now. Marvellous. I'll find out by Tuesday.
outcome_lines.refused: Then I'll keep both and bow to both. Safest, really.

chapters.line: She's out! Took a bow, said four years was a bit cramped, and left on tour.

outcome_lines.done: It's only a box now. She sends her love, and a signed photo, upside down.
outcome_lines.refused: Then it's mine. I'll put the cat in. For old times' sake. Briefly.

chapters.line: This clock runs backwards. Since Tuesday. I've begun to feel peculiar.

outcome_lines.done: Capital. I'll take it with my own two hands. Look at these hands.
outcome_lines.refused: Keeping it, then. I can't say I mind. I've lost a few wrinkles.

chapters.line: Terribly sorry, I've lost my moustache. Or not yet grown it. Any books?

outcome_lines.done: A thousand thanks. I'll read about moustaches and think hard.
outcome_lines.refused: Then I shall wait for the moustache. I'm told it grows back. Eventually.

chapters.line: I'm at thirty, and the knees are marvellous. The clock won't stop, though.

outcome_lines.done: Good man. It's a pocket watch. I trust it. I trusted the last one.
outcome_lines.refused: Then I'll bring it back. I'll be younger. You may not recognise me.

chapters.line: I've stopped it at thirty. Excellent knees. Take the clock, ticking forwards.

outcome_lines.done: A pleasure, sir. I am off to dance. Badly, but with enormous vigour.
outcome_lines.refused: Then it ticks on my shelf. Slowly forward. Like a coward. Like a man.

chapters.line: I hunt ghosts. Mine is shy. It needs somewhere haunted to hide.

outcome_lines.done: It's already inside! It says thanks in cold spots. Lovely.
outcome_lines.refused: Then it'll keep hiding behind my sofa. I'm running out of sofa.

chapters.line: She moved into a snow globe. It snows in my lounge. Indoors.

outcome_lines.done: Take her! She's a lovely lodger, but she shakes herself at dawn.
outcome_lines.refused: I'll buy a bigger umbrella. And a shovel. For the sofa.

chapters.line: She's lonely, bless her. She wants a ring, to feel like someone's.

outcome_lines.done: Wonderful. She says it's the nicest thing a living person has done.
outcome_lines.refused: I'll tell her it's coming. She waits well. She's had practice.

chapters.line: She got a job at the library, shushing. She's never been happier.

outcome_lines.done: It was hers, a library watch. Always a minute fast. She wants you to have it.
outcome_lines.refused: Then it's mine. We'll be shushed together. I'm told it's an honour.
